categories.main_business_segments: Tayca Corporation operates two main business segments: Functional Materials (including titanium dioxide, fine particle titanium dioxide, fine particle zinc oxide, and surface-treated products) and Electronic Materials & Chemicals (including piezoelectric materials, conductive polymer agents, surfactants, sulfuric acid, and environmentally friendly anti-corrosion pigments). The group also has an 'Other' segment focused on logistics and engineering services related to its products.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company's core technologies include advanced particle size and shape control, surface treatment, and dispersion technologies for inorganic powders, especially titanium dioxide. It also leverages proprietary methods in piezoelectric single crystal growth, conductive polymer synthesis, and surfactant formulation, with ongoing R&D in high-transparency UV filters, environmentally friendly materials, and high-performance electronic components.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Tayca serves a diverse customer base across industries such as cosmetics (UV filters and functional additives), paints and coatings, plastics, printing inks, electronics (capacitors, sensors, medical devices), and daily consumer goods (detergents). Major end markets include automotive, IT/electronics, healthcare, and consumer products.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in Japan, with significant manufacturing and sales presence in Thailand, Vietnam, and the United States. Its products are sold globally, with key markets in Asia, Europe, and North America.
categories.supply_chain_position: Tayca operates mainly as a midstream supplier, manufacturing specialty chemicals, functional materials, and electronic materials that are integrated into customers' end products. It also provides upstream raw materials and downstream logistics and engineering services within its group.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, Tayca is focusing on expanding its presence in high-growth areas such as cosmetic ingredients and electronic materials, aiming for global niche leadership. R&D priorities include developing high-value specialty chemicals, environmentally friendly and sustainable materials, and advanced electronic components, with an emphasis on innovation, process improvement, and carbon neutrality.
categories.revenue_model: The company primarily generates revenue through the sale of manufactured products (chemicals, materials, and electronic components) to industrial customers. It also earns income from logistics, warehousing, and engineering services provided to group companies and external clients.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Tayca competes with global and domestic chemical/materials manufacturers such as Ishihara Sangyo, Sakai Chemical, and multinational chemical firms in the functional materials and electronic materials sectors. It positions itself as a global niche leader in cosmetic ingredients and medical piezoelectric materials, leveraging proprietary technologies and high-quality standards.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, Tayca reported consolidated sales of 55.7 billion yen and net income attributable to parent shareholders of 2.4 billion yen, with a workforce of 838 employees. The company has demonstrated steady growth, with a 5.2% year-on-year increase in sales and a 29.8% increase in net income, and targets further expansion to 68 billion yen in sales and 9%+ operating margin by FY2027.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Tayca emphasizes high-performance, safety, and environmental compatibility in its products, offering advanced functional materials with superior transparency, UV protection, and sensory properties for cosmetics, as well as high-reliability electronic materials for automotive and medical applications. Its differentiation lies in proprietary technologies, global niche focus, and the ability to provide tailored solutions to meet evolving customer and regulatory demands.
